composition.pileCenter: min(48cqh - header height, available table height + hand headroom - half pile height - 12px); at height <=300px: 45cqh - header height
composition.hand: Full-height lower scrollport extends below the clipped page through a measured negative bottom margin; deepest resting fan corner crops about 25% of native face height. Inner and legally raised cards expose more. Horizontal overflow only; 44px independent paging gutters.

overlap.source: lib/handLayout.ts getHandOverlap; GameBoard ResizeObserver subtracts scrollport padding and ignores hidden zero-size measurements, preserving the last stable fit
overlap.minimumAdvance: min(card width, max(44px, 40% of card width))
overlap.fit: Clamp available advance to the minimum/preferred range. Overflow scrolls without changing card size.

handClearance.inspectionLift: 30.5px * hand scale + 8px; same for keyboard focus
handClearance.restingStack: Legal cards retain z-index 0; ordinary legal idle breathe removed.
handClearance.focusInspectionHover: Suppress extra hover lift and growth; reveal the complete face without vertical hand/document scrolling.

crop.source: lib/handLayout.ts getHandFan and getHandCropMargin; components/HandCard.tsx shares fan angle/drop; GameBoard measures native face offsetWidth/offsetHeight
crop.target: Deepest resting corner loses about 25% of native face height; inner and legally raised cards expose more.
crop.fan: angle = fromCenter * min(5, 12 / half); drop = 520 * (1 - cos(angle)) + edge^2 * 16
crop.fanModifiers: depth 0.45 / rotation 0.5 by default; depth 0.2 / rotation 0.3 at height <=600px
crop.cornerExcursion: fan drop * depth + native width / 2 * sin(abs(fan angle * rotation)) + native height * 0.2 * (1 - cos(abs(fan angle * rotation)))
crop.application: Negative scrollport bottom margin; full face remains within the actual scrollport while the page clips its lower quarter.
crop.angleUnits: Fan angles are degrees; convert to radians for sin/cos.

controls.desktop: Centered turn/inspection toolbar with independent right UNO/Pass slots.
controls.height <=600px: Turn cue left and actions right of a 200px central pile lane; inspection uses its own bounded lane below badges.
controls.height <=360px: 180px central pile lane; Draw inset at top of card back and written chosen wild color inset at bottom of discard.
controls.targets: 44px paging, inspection dismiss and contextual actions
controls.height <=300px: Pile scale 0.6; center at 45cqh minus header height; upper seats top -8px and flank seats top 6%; ordinary enabled draw-pile parent animation none.

segments.scope: Board and native game dialogs occupy reported first uninterrupted segment; dialogs inset 12px.
segments.orientation: Exact window.viewport.segments first panel, then CSS segment arrangement fallback, then viewport; width <=700px and height >width gates play.
segments.fallback: Ordinary responsive viewport without segment reporting.
segments.evidenceLimit: Panel-sized captures do not certify physical hinge/touch behavior or runtime reduced-motion execution. Quarter-hand finish review: ship, zero material fixes.

narrative.overview:
A welcoming shared card table combines a rich blue field, warm cream foreground, vivid native UNO cards and expressive illustrated human portraits. Outfit keeps the interface friendly and direct; Barlow Condensed gives the deck, wordmark and selected game actions their familiar energy. Soft contact shadows and inset press edges make cards and controls feel physical.

This records the shipped October 24 composite: Classic supplies the blue field and card prominence, Color court supplies the portraits, and After-hours supplies amber turn and action emphasis. The approved direction is `.impeccable/review/experience-reset/contract.md` (FORM seed `2fba311c`); its three references are `reset-classic.png`, `reset-color-court.png` and `reset-after-hours.png` under `.impeccable/mocks/decision/`. No catalog quality-bar world was selected. Earlier Comic-card showdown, giant-cast/painted-menu, violet-corner, illustrated-room and poker-table instructions are historical and superseded. Their assets and provenance remain recoverable; they are not current surface guidance.
keyCharacteristics: Quiet blue, charcoal/crimson or plum edition fields keep attention on live cards and people.
Human portraits, opaque nameplates and exact hand counts make the table social and readable.
Outfit UI and Barlow Condensed deck lettering share one friendly voice.
Amber pressed actions and a compact real countdown explain the current decision.
A quarter-cropped curved held hand preserves direct legal play, readable overlap and independent large-hand scrolling.

rules.name: The Published Color Rule
rules.body: Amber, cream active badges, legal-card outlines and wild swatches describe actual published state. Retain names, counts and written action/color labels alongside color.

rules.name: The Two Lettering Roles Rule
rules.body: Outfit carries ordinary interface headings. Condensed italic lettering belongs to brand/deck expression and the existing emphatic game actions; it is not a global heading transform.

rules.name: The Hand Owns Its Width Rule
rules.body: Fit by overlap alone: retain an exposed strip of at least 44px or the full card width when smaller. A large hand scrolls at the panel's existing face size; hand count never shrinks cards or creates document-width overflow. The owner-requested bottom-quarter crop is independent of count and compensates for the fan corners.

rules.name: The Uninterrupted Panel Rule
rules.body: Keep identities, piles, the exposed held hand and native game dialogs within the first reported usable segment; only the intentional lower-quarter crop crosses its bottom edge. Place compact controls in reserved lanes so no identity, label or decision covers a card face.

rules.name: The Reachable Decision Rule
rules.body: In setup, room, account and help flows, scroll the content body while keeping the primary decision or lesson navigation visible. Short-height adjustments preserve target size and readable content instead of shrinking the entire panel.

rules.name: The One Open Task Rule
rules.body: Keep optional identity, progress and social controls behind the avatar. Show the four-choice settings overview or one selected task; mount optional progress and pickers when opened. Ready-made profile portraits remain immediately visible. The current task keeps its heading and decision reachable; custom-profile drafts use their own native dialog and explicit save/cancel boundary.

rules.name: The Contact Rule
rules.body: Use inset press depth for actions and stock/contact depth for cards. Preserve readable resting geometry and keyboard focus; sound and animation never determine turn timing.

rules.name: The Distinct State Rule
rules.body: The active check identifies the selected profile; the star identifies a home favorite. Saving a custom draft is the explicit boundary before its rules become active.

dos: **Do** use the quiet edition field, warm cream, human portraits and vivid native deck as one shared identity.
**Do** keep Outfit ordinary headings and the separate Barlow Condensed brand/deck roles.
**Do** retain saved appearances on other dialogs, the avatar popover and invitation notices, while keeping Settings warm-white with navy text.
**Do** keep exact hand counts, inline compact status, a real turn clock and written action/color cues.
**Do** preserve the quarter-cropped curved held hand, readable overlap, independent overflow, direct legal play and visible keyboard focus.
**Do** keep compact cues, inspection and actions clear of identities and piles, and confine game dialogs to the reported usable panel.
**Do** keep setup, account and help decisions outside the scrolling content body, and distinguish actual table rules from practice examples.
**Do** show the four-choice settings overview or one task, keep ready-made portraits visible, and expose rule controls only inside a named custom-profile draft.
**Do** use soft contact depth and the intentional inset amber pressed-control lip.
**Do** keep original artwork and exact provenance, even when earlier artwork is superseded.
**Do** verify six-seat landscape phones, large hands and reduced motion when extending the interface.
donts: **Don't** restore giant background cast, painted menu-card actions, ink swashes, poker felt/rail or the giant orbit field.
**Don't** add decoration behind the piles or allow compact player states to expand into their space.
**Don't** add another font family, glyph icons, mixed display systems or a parallel component library.
**Don't** replace the live deadline with a decorative countdown or reset it after a draw or metadata update.
**Don't** add blocking splashes or let audio, reactions or motion gate game turns.
**Don't** repeat identity editors in joining or room setup, or add routine hand coaching.
**Don't** offer Stack party or Wild table as built-in choices; use named custom profiles for house rules.
**Don't** label Flip or Flex playable before their actual decks/actions exist, or describe the three originals as editable house-rule presets.
